newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ZOLA CONFIDENT ABOUT PARTNERING VIERI.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZOLA CONFIDENT ABOUT PARTNERING VIERI.

text.p: Italy's inspirational striker Gianfranco Zola has no worries about playing alongside uncapped Juventus attacker Christian Vieri in Saturday's World Cup qualifier against Moldova.

Injuries to Pier Luigi Casiraghi and Fabrizio Ravanelli have left Italian coach Cesare Maldini little option but to draft in the uncapped Vieri as partner for Zola, who now plays his club soccer with English side Chelsea.

Italy beat Moldova 3-1 away, leading to expectations of a possible goalscoring feast at home and the likelihood that Zola or Vieri will end the night as the man who scored Italy's 1,000th international goal since the first in 1910.
Zola scored Italy's 997th in 541 official matches with the winner against England at Wembley in February.
Speaking at team training, the little Sardinian predicted there would be no problems partnering 23-year-old Vieri.

"Christian's tactical awareness has surprised me...He's very similar to Casiraghi and I will have to play off and around him but I don't think there'll be any problems of understanding between us," he said.
"I've given him just one piece of advice, and that is to play according to his instinct."
Zola's winning goal in the group two qualifier against England at Wembley left Italy joint top with England but with a game in hand. They should go top on Saturday.
Apart from Vieri, the only other change from the side which beat England is the inclusion of Lazio player Alessandro Nesta instead of Parma's Fabio Cannavaro.
Nesta's inclusion is an inevitable reflection of the fact that Maldini expects Moldova to play a defensive game, leaving the Italian defence free to move forward, a point also underlined by Zola.

"The game against Moldova is easy only on paper. Our opponents will close up in numbers in front of their goalkeeper, leaving the initiative to us," Zola said. "We'll have to be good and score early."
Saturday's qualifier in the north-eastern port of Trieste, birthplace of Maldini, is the first of two group two games played by Italy in the next week. They face Poland in Chorzow on April 2.
Moldova are bottom of the group having lost all three games so far, beaten at home by England and Italy and away by Poland.
Italy - Angelo Peruzzi, Alessandro Costacurta, Alessandro Nesta, Ciro Ferrara, Paolo Maldini, Angelo Di Livio, Demetrio Albertini, Roberto Di Matteo, Dino Baggio, Gianfranco Zola, Christian Vieri.
Moldova - Denis Romanenco, Vitali Culibaba, Vasile Toloconicov, Ion Testimetanu, Oleg Fistican, Alexandr Curtianu, Marin Spinu, Oleg Sischin, Sergiu Epureanu, Alexandr Popovici, Serghei Clescenco.
